pull.title: test: fix waitTipChanged timeout on slow hosts and use monotonic clock in interface_ipc_mining
pull.body:
Follow up suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36731#issuecomment-6675432663.

The first commit fix the timeout on a slow host and the second one use time.monotonic() for durations.

Note (added after merge): the first commit's failure is not a wall clock problem. The faketime command only reproduces it by making the test slow. See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4565751670 

Command to reproduce the errors with a simulated slow wall clock:
```
faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.1" build/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
```

Code review ACK 46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4. This makes `interface_ipc_mining.py` more robust than on master: duration checks no longer fail when the system clock steps (like hebasto's NetBSD run, where the measured duration came out negative), and the `waitTipChanged` call that waits for a mined block no longer has only 1 second (with the default timeout factor) for the test to mine it.

I also ran the faketime command from the description: master fails at "Mine a block" and this PR passes. This is only a partial fix, though: the `waitNext` fee-increase wait has the same race and isn't changed, because the faketime repro can't trigger it (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4565761925). It would be good to fix this case as well.

comments.body:
In commit "test: fix waitTipChanged timeout on slow hosts in interface_ipc_mining" (9b6dadb39c22bfb6d8b8040519316768919ff906)

Nit: could the commit message explain what goes wrong? It only has a subject line now, and the PR description's faketime repro makes it look like a wall clock problem, which isn't what this commit fixes. Maybe something like:

> Use a 1 minute timeout for the waitTipChanged call that waits for a newly mined block, instead of default_ipc_timeout, which is only 1 second when the test runs with the default --timeout-factor (CI uses 40).
>
> The test sends waitTipChanged, waits 0.1 seconds, and then calls generate. Everything between the node receiving the request and the new block becoming its tip (the rest of that sleep, the generate RPC, and creating, validating and connecting the block) had to fit in that 1 second, which a busy machine may not manage. When it didn't, waitTipChanged returned the old tip and the height check failed. The longer timeout costs nothing when the test passes, because the call returns as soon as the tip changes.

As for why the faketime command reproduces this: it triggers the same failure, but not through the wall clock. The node measures the `waitTipChanged` deadline with the [steady clock](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4/src/node/block_template_manager.cpp#L235), which `--exclude-monotonic` [leaves alone](https://github.com/wolfcw/libfaketime/blob/03a2fdee4d6fef55e8f58451192cc0cadebd5f77/man/faketime.1#L37-L38) (it tells faketime not to fake `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`). But libfaketime also stretches `epoll_wait` timeouts, so the `asyncio.sleep(0.1)` in [`wait_and_do`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4/test/functional/test_framework/ipc_util.py#L48-L68) takes a full second of real time and uses up the timeout before the block is mined. On master, shrinking that sleep makes "Mine a block" pass under faketime, and raising it to 1 second makes it fail the same way without faketime. So for this commit, faketime is just a way to make the test slow. It also means the repro misses the same race in the `waitNext` fee-increase wait, which this PR doesn't fix: `waitNext` measures its deadline with the [wall clock](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4/src/node/block_template_manager.cpp#L119-L120), which faketime slows down along with the sleep (see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4565761925).

In commit "test: fix waitTipChanged timeout on slow hosts in interface_ipc_mining" (9b6dadb39c22bfb6d8b8040519316768919ff906)

This PR fixes only one of two places with the same race. This `waitNext` call waits for an event the test triggers after `wait_and_do`'s 0.1s sleep, just like the "Mine a block" `waitTipChanged` call the commit fixes, and its timeout is also `default_ipc_timeout` (1 second with the default `--timeout-factor`). If the sleep, the RPC and the mempool update together take more than a second, `waitNext` times out and `assert template6 is not None` fails. I checked this by passing `sleep_time=1.2` to this `wait_and_do` call, which makes the test fail at that assert.

The faketime repro only catches the `waitTipChanged` case because the two methods use different clocks: `waitTipChanged` measures its deadline with the [steady clock](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4/src/node/block_template_manager.cpp#L235), which faketime leaves running at real speed, while `waitNext` uses the [wall clock](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4/src/node/block_template_manager.cpp#L119-L120), which faketime slows down along with the sleep, so the deadline stretches too and the test still passes.

Could use the long timeout here as well. It might be simplest to set it once in `run_test` next to `default_ipc_timeout`:

```python
# Timeout for waits that should return early because of an event the test
# triggers, long enough not to expire on a slow host.
self.long_ipc_timeout = max(self.default_ipc_timeout, 60000.0)  # at least 1 minute
```

and use it for both `waitTipChanged` calls, this wait, and the existing `max(self.default_ipc_timeout, 60000.0)` in `wait_for_block()`. The `template2` wait (`2000.0 * timeout_factor` with a `1.1 * timeout_factor` sleep) has a similar but smaller window and could use it too, since it ignores fees and only returns for the tip update.
